title: S-GAP: Stealthy Graph Attack Primitives for Graph Large Language Models

paragraphs.en: Graph Large Language Models (GraphLLMs) enable powerful semantic understanding and reasoning over Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs), while their semantic reasoning may exhibit vulnerabilities to perturbations in node text and graph structure under adversarial attack evaluation. Existing attacks typically construct textual and structural perturbations in separate stages guided by distinct realization intents. However, this separation results in attack-intent fragmentation , causing semantic incoherence between the two perturbation types, thereby undermining attack stealth and making them easier for GraphLLMs to identify and disregard, ultimately weakening attack effectiveness. To avoid attack-intent fragmentation , we propose the Graph Attack Primitive (GAP), an atomic semantic representation that unifies textual and structural perturbations under a coherent attack intent. By carefully calibrating the semantic composition of a GAP, we can achieve strong attack effectiveness while maintaining sufficient attack stealth. Furthermore, we introduce S-GAP ( S tealthy GAP ), a multi-agent framework that iteratively refines the semantic content of the GAP. The framework unifies GAP planning and realization and continuously refines this process through surrogate evaluation and textual feedback. Extensive experiments across four datasets, three GraphLLMs, and two attack settings show that S-GAP improves ASR over the strongest baselines by 7.02% on average while producing more relationally plausible perturbations, exposing critical vulnerabilities in current GraphLLMs and motivating more robust defenses.

paragraphs.en: Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs), which integrate graph structure with textual content, are widely used to represent citation networks ( Tang et al. 2024 ) , product networks ( Fan et al. 2022 ) , and other knowledge-rich networks ( Zhong et al. 2023 ; Ying et al. 2026 ) . Recently, Graph Large Language Models (GraphLLMs) ( Chen et al. 2024 ; Wang et al. 2024 ; Zhang et al. 2026 ) have incorporated the powerful semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities of large language models into graph learning, enabling joint reasoning over node text and graph structure. Compared with conventional graph models, this integration allows GraphLLMs to contextualize node semantics using relational information, supporting richer and more context-sensitive graph reasoning. However, this joint reliance also creates a coupled vulnerability: malicious text can distort node semantics, while manipulated relations can alter how those semantics are contextualized. Understanding how this coupled vulnerability can be exploited by adversarial attacks is therefore critical to the safe and reliable deployment of GraphLLMs in knowledge-intensive and decision-sensitive applications ( Gao et al. 2025 ; Dai et al. 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 文本属性图（Text-Attributed Graphs，TAGs）将图结构与文本内容相结合，被广泛用于表示引用网络（Tang 等人，2024）、产品网络（Fan 等人，2022）以及其他富含知识的网络（Zhong 等人，2023；Ying 等人，2026）。 近期，图大语言模型（Graph Large Language Models，GraphLLMs）（Chen 等人，2024；Wang 等人，2024；Zhang 等人，2026）已将大语言模型强大的语义理解和推理能力融入图学习中，从而实现了对节点文本和图结构的联合推理。 与传统图模型相比，这种整合使 GraphLLMs 能够利用关系信息为节点语义提供上下文，从而支持更丰富且更具上下文敏感性的图推理。 然而，这种联合依赖也产生了一种耦合的脆弱性：恶意文本可能扭曲节点语义，而被操纵的关系则可能改变这些语义的上下文呈现方式。 因此，理解对抗性攻击如何利用这种耦合的脆弱性，对于在知识密集型和决策敏感型应用中安全、可靠地部署 GraphLLMs 至关重要（Gao 等人，2025；Dai 等人，2024）。

paragraphs.en: Graph adversarial attacks systematically expose the vulnerabilities of GraphLLMs through budget-constrained perturbations to graph data and commonly operate in two settings: Graph Injection Attack (GIA), which introduces adversarial nodes together with their incident edges, and Graph Modification Attack (GMA), which alters existing graph elements. Across these settings, conventional methods manipulate graph structure, vectorized node attributes, or both ( Zügner et al. 2018 ; Zügner and Günnemann 2019 ; Ju et al. 2023 ; Ma et al. 2026 ) . Attacks on TAGs impose an additional constraint: attribute perturbations must be realized as valid natural-language text while being coordinated with structural manipulations ( Lyu et al. 2025 ; Chen et al. 2026 ; Lei et al. 2024 ) . These methods typically construct textual and structural perturbations in separate stages, with each stage guided by a separately defined realization intent derived from the shared attack objective. For example, the structural stage ( Lyu et al. 2025 ) is driven by relational criteria, whereas the textual stage ( Lei et al. 2024 ) follows separately defined semantic constraints. Although both stages pursue the same ultimate attack objective, their stage-specific attack intents are defined by different realization criteria rather than explicitly unified. We refer to this separation as attack-intent fragmentation .
paragraphs.zh: 图对抗性攻击通过以预算为约束对图数据进行扰动，系统性地揭示了 GraphLLM 的脆弱性，并且通常在两种场景下运行：图注入攻击（GIA），即引入对抗性节点及其关联边；以及图修改攻击（GMA），即改变现有的图元素。 在这些场景中，传统方法会操纵图结构、向量化的节点属性或两者兼有（Zügner et al. 2018；Zügner and Günnemann 2019；Ju et al. 2023；Ma et al. 2026）。 对 TAGs 的攻击附加了额外约束：属性扰动必须表现为有效的自然语言文本，并且需与结构操纵相协调（Lyu et al. 2025；Chen et al. 2026；Lei et al. 2024）。 这些方法通常在独立阶段构建文本和结构扰动，每个阶段都由一个基于共享攻击目标单独定义的实现意图所引导。 例如，结构阶段（Lyu et al. 2025）由关系性标准驱动，而文本阶段（Lei et al. 2024）则遵循单独定义的语义约束。 尽管两个阶段都追求相同的最终攻击目标，但它们各自特定的攻击意图是由不同的实现标准定义的，而非明确统一。 我们将这种分离称为“攻击意图碎片化”。

paragraphs.en: Attack-intent fragmentation can lead to semantic incoherence between textual and structural perturbations, with the generated text failing to justify the manipulated relations and the structural perturbations failing to support the adversarial semantics introduced by the text. Such incoherent perturbations lack sufficient attack stealth, making them more likely to be judged semantically implausible or weakly relevant and subsequently disregarded by the LLM components of GraphLLMs, ultimately weakening attack effectiveness. We further validate this observation by prompting an LLM to assess the plausibility of the relations produced by each attack and categorize them as low, medium, or high plausibility. As shown in Figure 1 , existing attacks produce substantially larger proportions of low-plausibility relations than the clean graph under both attack settings, suggesting that their textual and structural perturbations frequently form semantically implausible relations. In contrast, our method S-GAP yields plausibility distributions much closer to the clean reference, indicating that its perturbations better preserve the relational plausibility profile of the original graph and thus achieve stronger attack stealth.
paragraphs.zh: 攻击意图的碎片化可能导致文本扰动与结构扰动之间出现语义不连贯：生成的文本无法为被操纵的关系提供合理解释，而结构扰动也无法支持文本所引入的对抗性语义。 这类不连贯的扰动缺乏足够的攻击隐蔽性，因此更可能被判断为语义上不合理或相关性较弱，进而被 GraphLLMs 中的 LLM 组件忽略，最终削弱攻击效果。 我们通过提示一个 LLM 来评估每次攻击所生成关系的合理性，并将其分为低、中、高合理性三个等级，以进一步验证这一观察结果。 如图 1 所示，在两种攻击设置下，现有攻击产生的低合理性关系比例均显著高于干净图，这表明其文本扰动与结构扰动经常形成语义上不合理的关系。 相比之下，我们的方法 S-GAP 产生的合理性分布更接近干净的参考图，说明其扰动能更好地保留原始图的关系合理性特征，从而实现了更强的攻击隐蔽性。

paragraphs.en: To avoid attack-intent fragmentation, we propose the Graph Attack Primitive (GAP), an atomic semantic representation that provides a coherent attack intent shared by textual and structural perturbations. By explicitly specifying the target semantics to preserve and the adversarial semantics to introduce, a GAP can avoid semantically implausible perturbations while retaining adversarial strength. However, balancing these competing semantic compositions is inherently target-dependent and difficult to achieve in a single generation step. We therefore introduce S-GAP ( S tealthy GAP ), a multi-agent framework that iteratively refines GAPs through surrogate evaluation and textual feedback. The Planner Agent proposes a GAP for the target, which the Attack Agent instantiates as a concrete text–structure perturbation and evaluates using a surrogate GNN. The Main Agent controls the overall process and uses the target context and execution outcome to construct a textual feedback that guides the Planner Agent’s refinement in the next round.

paragraphs.en: We identify attack-intent fragmentation in adversarial attacks, where textual and structural perturbations guided by independent attack intents undermine stealth, and propose GAP, which provides a unified attack intent for both perturbation types and is expressively complete over the defined attack search space.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在对抗性攻击中识别出攻击意图的碎片化问题：由独立攻击意图引导的文本和结构扰动会破坏攻击的隐蔽性。为此，我们提出了 GAP 方法，该方法为两种类型的扰动提供了统一的攻击意图，并且在所定义的攻击搜索空间内具有充分的表达能力。

paragraphs.en: We introduce S-GAP, a multi-agent framework for unified target-specific GAP planning and realization with iterative feedback-guided refinement through surrogate evaluation and textual feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 S-GAP，这是一个多智能体框架，用于统一的目标特定 GAP 规划与实现，并通过代理评估和文本反馈进行迭代反馈引导的优化。

paragraphs.en: We conduct comprehensive experiments on four datasets with three victim GraphLLMs under two attack settings. The results demonstrate superior attack effectiveness and stealth over existing methods, exposing fundamental vulnerabilities in the joint textual and structural reasoning of current GraphLLMs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在四个数据集上，针对三种受攻击的 GraphLLM，在两种攻击设置下进行了全面的实验。 实验结果表明，该方法在攻击有效性和隐蔽性方面均优于现有方法，揭示了当前 GraphLLM 在文本与结构联合推理中的根本性漏洞。

paragraphs.en: Graph adversarial attacks traditionally manipulate graph topology or vectorized node attributes. In the graph injection setting, attackers ( Chen et al. 2022 ) introduce adversarial nodes together with their incident edges. TDGIA ( Zou et al. 2021 ) jointly optimizes injected features and connectivity to increase their influence on target predictions, while reinforcement-learning-based approaches ( Sun et al. 2020 ; Ju et al. 2023 ; Zhao and Zhang 2025 ) formulate node injection as a sequential decision process under different levels of model access. In the graph modification setting, attacks ( Li et al. 2021 ; Xu et al. 2022 ) alter existing graph elements: Nettack ( Zügner et al. 2018 ) constructs targeted local perturbations by modifying edges and node attributes, Metattack ( Zügner and Günnemann 2019 ) formulates graph poisoning as a meta-learning problem, and PRBCD ( Geisler et al. 2021 ) improves the scalability of structural attacks through randomized block coordinate descent. Despite their different threat models and optimization strategies, these methods operate primarily on graph topology and discrete or continuous feature representations, rather than directly constructing or editing the underlying natural-language text.
paragraphs.zh: 图对抗性攻击传统上会操纵图拓扑结构或向量化的节点属性。 在图注入场景中，攻击者（Chen 等人，2022）会引入对抗性节点及其关联边。 TDGIA（Zou 等人，2021）联合优化注入的特征和连接关系，以增强它们对目标预测的影响；而基于强化学习的方法（Sun 等人，2020；Ju 等人，2023；Zhao 和 Zhang，2025）则将节点注入建模为在不同模型访问权限下的序列决策过程。 在图修改场景中，攻击方法（Li 等人，2021；Xu 等人，2022）会改变现有图元素：Nettack（Zügner 等人，2018）通过修改边和节点属性来构建有针对性的局部扰动；Metattack（Zügner 和 Günnemann，2019）将图投毒问题建模为元学习问题；PRBCD（Geisler 等人，2021）则通过随机化块坐标下降法提升了结构攻击的扩展性。 尽管这些方法在威胁模型和优化策略上各不相同，但它们主要作用于图拓扑结构以及离散或连续的特征表示，而非直接构建或编辑底层的自然语言文本。

paragraphs.en: Recent studies extend graph attacks from vectorized attributes to textual and semantic perturbations on TAGs. WTGIA ( Lei et al. 2024 ) pioneers text-level graph injection by converting adversarial feature patterns into interpretable textual nodes. ATAG-LLM ( Lyu et al. 2025 ) further employs LLMs to generate candidate injection texts and uses graph explanations to determine their injection positions in a black-box setting. Beyond raw-text generation alone, GraphTextack ( Ma et al. 2026 ) jointly searches the connectivity and semantic feature assignments of injected nodes through evolutionary optimization. For graph modification, IMDGA ( Fan et al. 2026 ) combines graph-aware textual substitutions with edge pruning to improve attack effectiveness and stealthiness, while BadGraph ( Chen et al. 2026 ) leverages graph priors and LLM reasoning to jointly perturb textual semantics and topology. These studies establish textual semantics and graph structure as coupled attack surfaces. However, their semantic coordination is embedded in particular generation procedures and perturbation mechanisms, such as node injection, textual substitution, or topology modification. In contrast, S-GAP introduces the Graph Attack Primitive as an explicit semantic interface between attack intent and concrete text–structure realization, enabling the same representation to guide both GIA and GMA.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的研究将图攻击从向量化属性扩展到了对 TAGs 的文本和语义扰动。 WTGIA（Lei 等人，2024）通过将对抗性特征模式转换为可解释的文本节点，首次实现了文本层面的图注入。 ATAG-LLM（Lyu 等人，2025）进一步利用 LLM 生成候选注入文本，并通过图解释在黑盒环境中确定其注入位置。 除了单纯的原始文本生成外，GraphTextack（Ma 等人，2026）还通过进化优化联合搜索注入节点的连接性和语义特征分配。 在图修改方面，IMDGA（Fan 等人，2026）将感知图的文本替换与边修剪相结合，以提高攻击的有效性和隐蔽性；而 BadGraph（Chen 等人，2026）则利用图先验和 LLM 推理，联合扰动文本语义和拓扑结构。 这些研究确立了文本语义和图结构为相互耦合的攻击面。 然而，它们的语义协调被嵌入在特定的生成流程和扰动机制中，例如节点注入、文本替换或拓扑修改。 相比之下，S-GAP 引入了“图攻击原语”作为攻击意图与具体文本-结构实现之间的显式语义接口，使同一表示能够指导 GIA 和 GMA。

paragraphs.en: As illustrated in Figure 2 , S-GAP is a multi-agent framework that iteratively refines GAPs using surrogate evaluation and textual feedback. The Main Agent coordinates the process by maintaining the attack state and deciding whether refinement should continue or terminate. At each iteration, the Planner Agent composes or refines a GAP. The Attack Agent then generates setting-specific text–structure perturbations from the GAP and evaluates them using a surrogate GNN. The Main Agent then updates the attack state with the execution outcome and produces textual feedback to guide the Planner Agent’s next refinement.
paragraphs.zh: 如图 2 所示，S-GAP 是一个多智能体框架，它通过代理评估和文本反馈迭代优化 GAP。 主智能体通过维护攻击状态并决定优化过程是继续还是终止来协调整个流程。 在每次迭代中，规划智能体会构建或优化一个 GAP。 随后，攻击智能体根据该 GAP 生成特定于设置的文本-结构扰动，并使用代理 GNN 对其进行评估。 接着，主智能体用执行结果更新攻击状态，并生成文本反馈以指导规划智能体的下一次优化。

paragraphs.en: Table 1 shows that S-GAP achieves the highest ASR in all 24 cases, outperforming the strongest baseline by 12.78 and 1.25 percentage points on average under GMA and GIA, respectively. GMA is generally more effective because it directly modifies target nodes, whereas GIA is more practical but influences predictions indirectly through injected nodes. Baselines perform better in their native settings, suggesting limited adaptability across attack settings. In contrast, the unified GAP representation enables S-GAP to naturally adapt to both GIA and GMA, achieving consistently strong performance in both settings. Nettack, Mettack, PRBCD, and G2A2C mainly optimize structures or numerical features using GNN-oriented objectives, without explicitly modeling raw-text semantics. WTGIA, ATAG-LLM, and BadGraph incorporate textual information but depend on predefined features, similarity proxies, or fixed attack strategies, limiting the coordination between text and structure. In contrast, S-GAP directly models semantic attack intentions and uses execution feedback to jointly refine textual and structural perturbations, thereby avoiding reliance on numerical objectives or fixed proxies.

paragraphs.en: Table 1 shows that S-GAP achieves the highest relational plausibility across all datasets and settings. Structure-oriented attacks such as Nettack, Mettack, and PRBCD generally exhibit low plausibility because their edge perturbations lack semantic constraints; for example, Nettack achieves strong GMA ASR on Cora but only 4.89% High-Plaus. However, their separately optimized text and structure or fixed influencer strategies limit semantic alignment. paragraphs.en: To determine whether attack success arises from plausible adversarial evidence or anomalous relational shortcuts, we apply a relational-plausibility filter that reverts edge perturbations assigned scores of 1–2 while retaining the textual perturbations. Several baselines degrade substantially on Cora, indicating reliance on semantically unjustified relations. In contrast, changes on PubMed are minor because low-plausibility relations are rare. S-GAP retains at least 85.0% of its ASR and remains the strongest attack after filtering, showing that its effectiveness primarily arises from plausible text–structure interactions. Its slight improvement under PubMed GMA further suggests that some implausible relations may even interfere with the attack. Complete plausibility-score distributions and victim-specific post-filtering results are provided in the appendix.

paragraphs.en: To examine whether the confidence-drop score identifies perturbations likely to succeed on target GraphLLMs, we group attacks by their final scores and measure the victim-averaged proportion of successful attacks in each bin. Figure 4 shows that higher scores generally correspond to larger success proportions. The relatively low proportions reflect the prediction gap between the surrogate model and target GraphLLMs, while the overall trend confirms that the score remains informative of attack success.
paragraphs.zh: 为了检验置信度下降分数能否识别出可能在对目标 GraphLLM 成功实施的扰动，我们按最终分数对攻击进行分组，并测量每个分数区间内成功攻击的受害者平均比例。 图 4 显示，分数越高通常对应着更高的成功比例。 相对较低的成功比例反映了代理模型与目标 GraphLLM 之间的预测差异，而整体趋势则证实该分数仍然能够反映攻击的成功情况。

paragraphs.en: We compare S-GAP with three variants: w/o score removes confidence-drop scoring from the Attack Agent, w/o GAP removes the GAP entirely and directly generates candidate attack entities from the target context, and w/o feedback removes textual feedback, with no refinement of GAPs. paragraphs.en: We investigate vulnerabilities in GraphLLMs’ joint reasoning over textual attributes and graph structure in TAGs. Existing attacks may underexpose these vulnerabilities because attack-intent fragmentation misaligns textual and structural perturbations, weakening stealth and effectiveness. We therefore propose GAP to unify attack intent and develop S-GAP to iteratively refine and realize GAPs through multi-agent planning, surrogate evaluation, and textual feedback. Across all 24 combinations of four datasets, three GraphLLMs, and two attack settings, S-GAP performs best in every case, outperforming the strongest baselines by 7.02% on average while producing more relationally plausible perturbations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了 GraphLLM 在 TAGs 中对文本属性和图结构进行联合推理时存在的漏洞。 现有的攻击方法可能未能充分暴露这些漏洞，因为攻击意图的碎片化导致文本扰动与结构扰动之间缺乏对齐，从而削弱了攻击的隐蔽性和有效性。 因此，我们提出了 GAP 以统一攻击意图，并开发了 S-GAP，通过多智能体规划、代理评估和文本反馈来迭代优化并实现 GAP。 在所有由四个数据集、三种 GraphLLM 和两种攻击设置构成的 24 种组合中，S-GAP 在每种情况下都表现最佳，平均比最强的基线模型高出 7.02%，同时生成的扰动在关系上也更具合理性。
